blocks.text: 79 הַפְטָרָה לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 79

uncertainties: I can't tell exactly where the holam sits in שִׁלֹ֑ו: it could be over the lamed or on the vav. The etnah under the lamed is clear.
The conjunctive accent under the bet of וַיָּבִ֥אוּ is read as merkha; it is small.

blocks.text: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י חֵ֥י נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אֲדֹנִ֑י אֲנִ֣י הָֽאִשָּׁ֗ה הַנִּצֶּ֤בֶת עִמְּכָה֙ בָּזֶ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
uncertainties: The long horizontal stroke before the first אֲדֹנִ֔י is the font stretching the aleph to fill the line. It is not a paseq or an accent.
The conjunctive accent on חֵ֥י is read as merkha; it is faint.

blocks.text: אֶל־הַנַּ֥עַר הַזֶּ֖ה הִתְפַּלָּ֑לְתִּי וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ אֶת־שְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתִּי מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃
uncertainties: The mark over the tav of וַיִּתֵּ֨ן is read as qadma.
שְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י is spelled defectively, as printed.

blocks.text: וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י הִשְׁאִלְתִּ֙הוּ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כָּל־הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֔ה ה֥וּא שָׁא֖וּל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ שָׁ֖ם לַֽיהוָֽה׃
uncertainties: The he of הִשְׁאִלְתִּ֙הוּ֙ is printed stretched. The double pashta is visible.
The conjunctive accent under ה֥וּא is read as merkha; it is faint.

blocks.text: וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל חַנָּה֙ וַתֹּאמַ֔ר עָלַ֤ץ לִבִּי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה רָ֥מָה קַרְנִ֖י בַּֽיהוָ֑ה רָ֤חַב פִּי֙ עַל־א֣וֹיְבַ֔י כִּ֥י שָׂמַ֖חְתִּי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
uncertainties: The meteg in each בַּֽיהוָ֔ה / בַּֽיהוָ֑ה is small but appears to be there.
The munach under the aleph of א֣וֹיְבַ֔י is faint.

blocks.text: אֵין־קָד֥וֹשׁ כַּיהוָ֖ה כִּי־אֵ֣ין בִּלְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר כֵּאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
uncertainties: This print has a maqaf in כִּי־אֵ֣ין. I can't tell whether there is a meteg or another mark under the kaf.
The accent under the dalet of קָד֥וֹשׁ is read as merkha; it is small.

blocks.text: אַל־תַּרְבּ֤וּ תְדַבְּרוּ֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה יֵצֵ֥א עָתָ֖ק מִפִּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל דֵּעוֹת֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְל֥א° נִתְכְּנ֖וּ עֲלִלֽוֹת׃
uncertainties: I can't tell whether the second גְבֹהָ֔ה (at the start of the line) has a dagesh in the gimel.
Over וְל֥א there is a qere circlet. The pointing printed on the ketiv is unclear: there may be a holam dot near the lamed, and the accent under it is read as merkha. See the separate qere block.

blocks.text: written: ולא ; read: ולו (marginal note printed: ולו ק׳)

uncertainties: The mark under the qof of קֶ֚שֶׁת is read as yetiv.
This print has a maqaf in אָֽזְרוּ־חָֽיִל. The mark under the aleph looks like a meteg; it might be merkha.

blocks.text: שְׂבֵעִ֤ים בַּלֶּ֙חֶם֙ נִשְׂכָּ֔רוּ וּרְעֵבִ֖ים חָדֵ֑לוּ עַד עֲקָרָה֙ יָלְדָ֣ה שִׁבְעָ֔ה וְרַבַּ֥ת בָּנִ֖ים אֻמְלָֽלָה׃
uncertainties: I can't see a dagesh in the lamed of חָדֵ֑לוּ in the scan.
I can't see a maqaf between עַד and עֲקָרָה֙. The words are printed with a wide space between them.
There may be a meteg in יָלְדָ֣ה; the mark is unclear.

blocks.text: יְהוָ֖ה מֵמִ֣ית וּמְחַיֶּ֑ה מוֹרִ֥יד שְׁא֖וֹל וַיָּֽעַל׃

uncertainties: The meteg under the mem of וּמַֽעֲשִׁ֑יר appears to be printed.

blocks.text: מֵקִ֨ים מֵעָפָ֜ר דָּ֗ל מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת֙ יָרִ֣ים אֶבְי֔וֹן לְהוֹשִׁיב֙ עִם־נְדִיבִ֔ים וְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד יַנְחִלֵ֑ם כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ מְצֻ֣קֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וַיָּ֥שֶׁת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם תֵּבֵֽל׃
uncertainties: I can't tell whether the kaf of כָב֖וֹד has a dagesh.
The meteg in מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת֙ and in לַֽיהוָה֙ is small.

blocks.text: רַגְלֵ֤י חֲסִידָו֙° יִשְׁמֹ֔ר וּרְשָׁעִ֖ים בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יִדָּ֑מּוּ כִּֽי־לֹ֥א בְכֹ֖חַ יִגְבַּר־אִֽישׁ׃
uncertainties: There is a qere circlet over חֲסִידָו֙. See the separate qere block.
I can't tell whether the bet of בְכֹ֖חַ has a dagesh.
The aleph of אִֽישׁ is printed stretched.

blocks.text: written: חסידו ; read: חסידיו (marginal note printed: דיו ק׳)
uncertainties: The marginal note shows only the ending ״דיו ק׳״. It is either an abbreviation of חסידיו or cut off at the edge of the scan.
The mark under the het of יֵחַ֣תּוּ is read as munach.

notes: The page is part of the haftarah for the first day of Rosh Hashanah: 1 Samuel 1:24 (end) to 2:10 (start). Every verse is fully pointed and has cantillation.
The Divine Name is printed יְהוָה with sheva and qamats and no holam throughout.
There are two qere notes. Both are marked with circlets in the text and notes in the outer margin: ולא/ולו in 2:3 and חסידו/חסידיו in 2:9.
The font stretches some letters to justify lines (aleph, he, final mem). Those strokes are not accents.
Where this print differs from common editions, I followed what is printed: it has a maqaf in כִּי־אֵין (2:2) and in אָזְרוּ־חָיִל (2:4), and I see no maqaf after עַד (2:5).
There are no prayers or rubrics on this page apart from the running header.
